source_row.rationale: Epidural anesthesia can produce maternal hypotension, decreasing uteroplacental perfusion and contributing to fetal late decelerations. Maternal blood pressure is therefore the priority assessment in this context. The other findings do not directly evaluate the immediate hemodynamic complication most likely to affect fetal oxygenation.
source_row.source_detail: Labor epidural monitoring/late decelerations discussion: neuraxial anesthesia can cause maternal hypotension; blood pressure and fetal heart rate require monitoring because reduced maternal pressure can reduce uteroplacental perfusion and contribute to fetal decelerations. Open RN Nursing Health Promotion 2e (2025), current NCBI Bookshelf content live-rechecked 2026-08-15; NCSBN 2026 Reduction of Risk Potential prioritization/monitoring check completed first. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: diagnostic/laboratory interpretation, postprocedure monitoring, device management and potential complications. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: Soon after labor epidural placement, the fetal tracing develops recurrent late decelerations. Which maternal assessment should the nurse prioritize?
